"Texture pattern" is an experiment about achieving colours with small lines forming a texture that you can alter. The piece is based on a grid system that is altered by a factor and in orientation, 3 mathematical sequences create a base rhythm. 

The colour palette is inspired by Riley's "La fête" with modifications and the monochrome version is based on 2 blacks and 2 whites.

In the live version, you can interact with your token using the following keys

's' saves a jpg
'1','2','3','4' sets the pixel density to 1,2,3,4
'+' adds 1000 lines per rectangle
'-' removes 1000 lines per rectangle
'n' allows you to toggle extra noise
'm' adds more noise
'b' removes some noise
'0' to toggle the background of each rectangle

Hash Smoke is an algorithm that generates drawings of smoke clouds.  Hash smoke clouds, to be exact.  It draws thousands of colorful, translucent circles that combine to form a sort of funky, puffy cloud.

The word “hash” in computer science is borrowed from cannabis culture.  Hashish has been made for thousands of years by chopping up and pressing the tasty parts of cannabis plants into a potent goop that can be carried around and smoked for fun.  Hash functions in computer science work the same way: they chop stuff up into unrecognizable goops so people can have more fun together.

Created by @capnganj – one love <3

A bespoke literary chance machine, crafted from a matrix of ranked, hand-crafted options.

Based on an original poem in four verses. 
This is part 2 - "The Lyre of the High". 
Parts 3-4 releasing concurrently. 

The algorithm that drives the poem is an evolving feature map. 
Each word has a series of features that, when selected, contribute to the selection of the following words.

In this way, the poem evolves in a way that is deterministic but with very random roots. 

The chance of two transactions generating the same poem from the system is about 1 in 450,000.

This work tries to explore and critique what "generative" art reallly means.

Is it generative to use existing manual art as a collage?
Is it generative art to take an existing picture and make the code paint every pixel manually?


This piece attempts go show that one can generate stylistic realist art using extremely simple code if the math is used effectively - showcasing my opinionated purist definition on the term "generative"


The four kinds of fruits, the bottle, the wood texture are all generated purely from minimal algorithmic code - totalling less than 200 lines for the core drawing code.

9295.d:
"VADFAD" is an experimental generative art piece that attempts to highlight some of the inherent contradictions surrounding the discussion of non-fungible tokens (NFTs) and its place as a vehicle for artistic creation, artistic expression and the potential of remuneration for artists.

p - pause

s - screenshot

To the extent possible, the source code is dedicated to the public domain (CC0) and can be used for any purpose, even commercial, by anyone. All third party libraries used are libre/free. Please check individual files for their respective licenses.

The hope is that the "VADFAD" NFT draws a parallel to other technological trends of the past and highlights how new technologies that are only just being understood, or experimented with, can have unforeseen benefits and whose enjoyment might seem obscure to an outside observer.

The video game arcade industry helped create video game empires, drive the adoption of home video consoles and advance the proliferation of personal computers. Just as video games of the past helped promote innovative new technologies, NFTs have the potential to drive innovation in other markets that aren't well understood or explored yet.

By combing a 1980s "8-bit" aesthetic, "VADFAD" tries to touch on the nostalgia for the arcade video game era of the 1980s while using a generative process to create almost surely unique 8-bit like monster creations. The combination of styles is done to try emphasize the similarity between the two eras, where the exuberance for the new technology, art and entertainment of the past has a similar spirit to the exhilaration of the present.

The price of this NFT piece is tailored to be approximately $0.25 United States dollars (USD). For the price of playing a typical 1980s video game arcade, anyone can mint this NFT.

This work hopes to add to the conversation about examining the reality of the ecosystem that we've developed around digital goods and intellectual property.

9321.d:
Out on the leading edge of the blockchain lies a multitude of new solar systems just waiting to be explored.

This generative art project uses p5.js to produce a representation of these solar systems using the transaction hash of your purchase.

Four values are determined when this piece is first purchased.
Star Type: M (Common), K (Uncommon), G (Uncommon), F (Uncommon), A (Uncommon), B (Uncommon), O (Rare), Black Hole (1%)
Number of Planets: 2 to 11 planets with an equal chance of generation
Number of Asteroid Belts*: None (Common), 1 (Uncommon), 2 (Rare), 3 (Very Rare)
Background**: Stars (Common), Galactic Arm (Uncommon), Nebula (Rare)

*The generation of an Asteroid Belt will replace a planetary orbit. E.g. A system that is generated with 10 planets and three asteroid belts will result in a system that contains seven planets and three asteroid belts.

** The background features generated use a seeded random value function and while they should conform to the standards of pseudorandom generation set forth by fx(hash), I am unable to guarantee that the exact position of 500+ objects are always going to generate in the exact position every time the project is loaded.

9335.d:
Each mint is audioreactive visuals paired with a beat that’s composed from a selection of audio tracks, all based on the transaction hash

The six “instruments” in this beat are features that pull from a set of possible variants. The beat that you end up with when you mint is layered together from those features: there’s 5x5x4x4x4x2 possibilities for the audio which is, like, a lot of possibilities

All of those audio tracks are composed by hand the old-fashioned human-made way using sampling, synths, soul, and Ableton Live

The visuals are driven by the instruments in the beat, the colors are straight up random, and the whole visual output is modified by another set of features that modulate resolution and lo-fi vibes

Click to toggle playing, and to see what rad visual moments you can pause the beat on

P5.js + chroma.js + Tone.js + beats

Void Wind is the first known work by Bytebites. It is an interactive, generative, 3D work inspired by the advancements in computer graphics in the mid-to-late 1900s. More specifically, this work is influenced by John Whitney’s motion graphics in the 1960s and other computer advancements at MIT during the 1970s. This work was built in javascript, using the three.js library.

Each piece is interactable by:
Left-click + dragging (or single finger drag) to rotate around scene
Scrolling (or pinching) to zoom in and out of scene.
Right-click dragging to pan around scene.

Many variables that make each instance of Wind in the Void unique and collectible. However, the following characteristics are notable demonstrations of rarity:

Stack
Single : common
Double : uncommon
Triple : rare

Background
Black : common
White : rare
Colored : very rare

Rainbow
0 : common
1 : rare
2 : very rare
3 : extremely rare

9394.d:
"Test Prints" are a result of the screen printing process. Before a print run, artists often test out new screens on scrap, or print directly on top of a former test so that no paper is wasted. Over time, compositions and colors of unrelated work are layered, creating a random and unique work. Test prints are often dinged, bent, scratched and smeared, adding to their character. The resulting 'monoprints' are often treasured by poster collectors due to their uniqueness and rarity. Some poster events invite artists to bring an old screen, and layers are then built up with random colors to see the resulting collaborative artwork. This generative artwork pays tribute to screen printing and the beauty of randomness.

Right-click the canvas and 'save image as' to export a 3072x4096 still.

Thank you all!
Artwork by 3dmanatee @3d_manatee. Made with p5js and ❤️.

This is the first iteration of a chess inspired series. Each piece was designed in a custom pixel editing tool and painted on a 16x16 chess board using p5.js. I plan to continue adding animations, color themes, autonomous battles and more...but each iteration will only be released if the previous iteration sells out.

Current iteration:
- Each design features 2-4 colors. (2 common, 3 uncommon, 4 rare)
- Pieces are randomly placed on the board using an algorithm designed to make the position feel like a real chess position. The algorithm is pretty basic. Kings can be adjacent to other kings, and other impossible chess positions can be generated.
- More pieces are more rare.
- There is a 1% chance of a "unicorn" color.

Future iteration ideas:
- Autonomous battles.
- Improved placement algorithm.
- More colors/themes.
- Improved animations.
- Variable board sizes.
- Board design iterations such as a coordinate system.
- More. Ping me on Twitter if you have ideas @RasterlyNFT

- A block is made up of a simple rectangle shape and a tiny rectangle inside of it.
- Use a grid-like system to distribute blocks from top to bottom, from left to right, but not strictly follow the grid.

- The distribution model produces varying results in rotation and spacing.
- For each block, it projects another rectangle with random size and rotation at the background, which extends its length to the bottom of the painting.
- There are lines behind the block which connect all of them together.

What a great thing it is to be young at heart. To be so blessed means, although you are an adult, you still retain the capacity for child-like delight in many things. You have not lost your capacity to be excited by little things, like the time a butterfly landed on your arm, or the gentle, protective feeling you get when a kitten jumps into your lap. Rainbows are beautiful, waterfalls are mesmerising, and it is exciting to get a call from an old friend. You still talk baby talk to all puppies.

The opposite of “young at heart” is to be “jaded.” Don’t become jaded; it’s really boring.

A heightmap is generated using fractal noise with different parameters and scales. Then we generate tens of thousands of paths by using a gradient descent algorithm with momentum, starting at random positions on the reversed heightmap. Those paths are then rendered using one of 11 different colour palettes.

Press "s" to save a screenshot.

Original artwork by William Watkins · Lyon, 2022

9459.d:
"I Stockpile Dreams With Tragedies : 1Gen" is an experimental generative art piece that is an attempt to highlight some of the inherent contradictions surrounding the discussion of non-fungible tokens (NFTs) and its place as a vehicle for artistic creation, artistic expression and the potential of remuneration for artists.

p - pause

s - screenshot

a - (advanced) record animation (5s)

To the extent possible, the source code is dedicated to the public domain (CC0) and can be used for any purpose, even commercial, by anyone. Third party libraries are used that are not CC0 licensed but have libre/free licensing terms that allow for commercial reuse (please see the LICENSE section for more details).

This work is influenced by stock art that is available from pay-to-download sites as well as drawing influence from other artists that have similar styles but don't make their art, or the code to generate it, libre/free.

Many times stock image sites that make available pictures similar to ones generated by this code can incur costs of $10 or more per image. Many sites offer monthly subscription rates starting at $50 per year. Price gouging, restrictive licensing and overly broad copyright terms are taken as the norm while technology that experiments with ideas of uniqueness, value and enabling alternative income streams is berated.

Why are stock image sites valuable but receiving payments from NFTs not?

"I Stockpile Dreams With Tragedies : 1Gen" is a continuation of "I Stockpile Dreams With Tragedies" incorporating additional basic shapes, shape selection and color.

This work hopes to add to the conversation about examining the reality of the ecosystem that we've developed around digital goods and intellectual property.

the sun will blind my eyes, i’ll love you anyway
thirsty for your smile, i watch you for a while
you are a vapour trail in a deep blue sky”

playing out different paths

trails between you and the faraway of everything

but here (now)

with luck
they lay next to you
and silently you appreciate each tick of the clock
wasted together
until life again gets in the way
and pulls you back
into the fray

The simplest colors from Mondrian's palette are then applied randomly in each square, to soothe and simplify the visual equation.

This is a mostly experimental artwork. I´ve discover this while travelling in the bus using the shader editor in android(wich i recommend cause is really really cool to make things fast). Those longs hours in the bus teach me weird techniques. 

This is based on a technique that accumulates feedback and once that passes certain limit(it depends on the edition) it decreases on another generative value(it deppens on the edition as well). Is rendered on a fragment shader in my p5.js system. 

This starts with the automatic mode where the drawing generates it selfs but once you click on the drawing you activate the manual mode. In the manual mode you can draw yourself. 

Controls in the manual mode : 
W : to clean screen. 
A : Hold it to make the pointer bigger. 
S : Hold it to make the pointer smaller. 


The variations comes in the way the automatic drawing is drawn and the limit and the decrease values (This affects the color palette).
